items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I left my guitar there because Leo Watson was there this night. And he wanted me to go to some after hours spot with him

ctx.x: (Inaudible) does not have a sense of humor necessary for jazz.

Oh, you have to have that, you know, and in order to survive, you know, you've got to have this because you're studying and you're hungry, you know, you're stranded. I've been stranded and I played with Roy. The first time I went on the road, I went to Roy's home town, Pittsburgh, and we played this club, this first night, and I left my guitar there because Leo Watson was there this night. And he wanted me to go to some after hours spot with him, and so I left my guitar then there and the club burned down. The…
I don't have any money, you know, nothing, stranded in this town. I've never been out of my hometown. Roy is there, he's stranded at home. So you've got to have a sense of humor.
